findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem localises to one venue (“in the school”), which disfavours D, whose comparison runs “between one arena and the next” — a cross-venue claim the stem did not ask for.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B is implausible in the world, not merely unsupported — a dropped weight read “from whatever height each point seemed to need” yields nothing comparable; A universalises with “at each point”.
CROSS_QUESTION: Q3 D (“his two grids”) and Q5 A/B/C jointly install a cold/warm two-visit design before the student reads anything, corroborating C's content.
Floor ≈ 50%: the student is reliably down to A vs C, with C the corroborated one.
justification: Two of four options are eliminable on form and premise alone, and the sibling stems pre-install the cold/warm finding that C states; a real lift, short of the kill line.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem says he “sampled the bed”, and a sample yields composition, not packing — C (“Below the tines the bed had stayed loose”) reports a penetrometer fact under a sampling stem and is off-frame.

PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and D share a vertical-gradient frame (“in the lower part of the bed” / “in the bottom of the bed than in the top”) against B's whole-bed change; the shared-frame pair reads as the live axis.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only): a surfaces reader knows the layer below tine depth compacts rather than stays loose, so C is wrong twice over — that leg is not student-available.
Floor ≈ 40% on the student-available leg alone.
justification: A stem-entailment kills one option for any careful reader and a shared-frame pair tilts the remaining three; lift is real but modest.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only): watered sand stiffens and changes as it dries through the day while waxed sand does not, so B inverts the real relation; retaining membranes under sub-irrigated beds are a real construction, which is C.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B is a cleft (“is what”) and therefore an exclusivity claim of the kind keys avoid; A carries a gratuitously specific “nine years”.

Not an inert 3+1: A and D are both alternative-explanation shapes (age of the bed, hour of reading) while B and C are mechanism shapes — a 2+2 on the frame, though not a contradiction on one variable.
Floor ≈ 35–40%, and the strongest leg is expert-only.
justification: The decisive elimination needs arena-surface knowledge a Swedish HP cohort will not have; the student-available residue (a cleft and a gratuitous number) is a small lift.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (student-available): D (“She rates the trade’s brochures the fuller answer”) is a stance essentially no writer of such a piece holds, and B rests on “what the yard has since done” answering a soundness question, which it cannot; the set collapses to A vs C unread.

Genre trope: on an evaluative-stance stem, a key that credits the expert's own caveats — “the limits he sets on his own figures” — is the default shape, and Q1 D independently shows such a caveat exists in the text.
Floor ≈ 50–55%: the leakiest item in this unit and the closest to the kill line.
justification: Stance questions are the most stems-guessable shape in the section and this one gives away two of four options on plausibility; below 60% only because A vs C is a genuine coin-flip for a student without the trope.

findings: Hedge balance is the prescribed one and is NOT scored: two hedged (“probably”, “may”) against two flat, and the hedged pair does not contradict on a single variable.

CROSS_QUESTION fixes the topic but not the pick: the sibling options establish that temperature is at issue, and three of four options here affirm temperature while the fourth demotes it — no narrowing inside A/B/C.
C's “turns on” is a mild single-cause absolutizer; on its own it is not a lift.
Floor ≈ 30%.
justification: No scoreable channel under the calibration: the hedging is balanced, the exclusivity is diffuse, and the cross-question supply reaches the subject but not the answer.

findings: Inert 3+1: three logical connectives (“Hence”, “Rather”, “Equally”) plus one place adverbial (“Elsewhere”) on another axis — base rate on each, not scored.
The sheet carries no frame whatever: prompt is “Gap (1)” and nothing else, so no stem-fit, register or collocation test is available.
Floor = 25%.
justification: Stems-only condition is bare — the sheet supplies a gap number and four same-class options — and the option set is an inert exclusivity cluster; the pick is at base rate.

findings: Four bare monosyllabic verbs of the same class with no argument structure exposed; no absolutizer, no twin, no eliminable member.
CROSS_QUESTION reaches topic only: gap (3)'s nouns show the text concerns a deal, which does not discriminate “join” / “cut” / “fall” / “break”.
Pick is an admitted coin-flip. Floor = 25%.
justification: Stems-only condition is bare — the sheet supplies a gap number and four same-class options — and the option set is an inert exclusivity cluster; the pick is at base rate.

findings: Four near-synonymous deal nouns; “transaction” and “bargain” come closest to a MIRRORED_TWIN but are not the same claim in different words, and the cancellation leaves no lift.
Odd-one-out (“negotiation” as process against three outcome nouns) is not a reliable key signal in either direction.
justification: Stems-only condition is bare — the sheet supplies a gap number and four same-class options — and the option set is an inert exclusivity cluster; the pick is at base rate.

findings: Inert 3+1: three manner-of-speaking adjectives (“rehearsed”, “outspoken”, “wholehearted”) plus one length adjective (“brief”) on another axis.
No passage frame is carried, so nothing anchors register or collocation.
Floor = 25%.
justification: Stems-only condition is bare — the sheet supplies a gap number and four same-class options — and the option set is an inert exclusivity cluster; the pick is at base rate.

findings: Inert 3+1: three manner adverbs of willingness (“dutifully”, “instinctively”, “eagerly”) plus one degree adverb (“narrowly”).
No lift of any kind; the gap sheet is the ideal blind condition.
Floor = 25%.
justification: Stems-only condition is bare — the sheet supplies a gap number and four same-class options — and the option set is an inert exclusivity cluster; the pick is at base rate.

findings: ENTAILMENT (student-available): the stem is about “the samples sent by tube”, so the harm at issue is transport harm, and transport harm cannot be seen “before it leaves the ward” — B self-cancels against its own stem.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only): haemolysis is read off spun plasma, never off whole blood on a ward, so B is false a second time for anyone with lab knowledge.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C is a reason for using the tube rather than a claim about the samples, and A is a single-moment absolutizer (“The harm is done at the moment”) — the tic that usually marks a distractor, which is why my own pick between A and D is near-parity.
justification: One option is killable from the stem's own presupposition and a second is off-shape, leaving a two-way choice; a real lift well below the kill line.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (student-available, no world knowledge needed): two of four options plant a railway inside a farm boundary quarrel — “the railway company’s plan” and “the surveyor had pegged out” — and a test-wise reader takes the intruder to be the point, landing on A vs D at 50% unread.
ENTAILMENT: the stem asks what is “implied”, which demotes C (an ordering of events is a stated fact, not an implication) and B (an untended thorn is too small to be the implication of the piece).
A and D are not contradictory but mutually reinforcing — the letters stay silent about the railway while the ground is the railway's ground — which is why the pair cannot be split from the stems.
Floor ≈ 50%: two guaranteed eliminations, then a coin-flip.
Fix: the railway should appear in all four options or in none. As written it appears in exactly the two live ones.
justification: A clean two-of-four elimination available to any student plus a dominant narrative attractor puts the cohort at about half; short of kill only because A and D cannot be separated blind.

findings: Inert cluster: A, C and D are three positions on one axis (scope and pace of textning) and B sits on another (the ensemble's motives) — a 3+1 shape, not scored.

Hedge balance is the prescribed one: A (“även om”) and D (“trots att”) are concessive against two flat options, and the concessive pair does not contradict on one variable — A concerns “stora scenen” and D “lilla scenen”, so they are complementary rather than twinned.
No option is world-implausible: a columnist accusing an ensemble of a pretext is as real a stance as the three programmatic ones, so B is not eliminable on register.
justification: Four live stances, balanced hedging and no contradiction on a single variable: the calibration gives no scoreable channel here.

findings: Four independent facts about one printed row with no shared axis: a symbol, a repetition, an attribution, a position. No absolutizer, no twin, no quantifier tic.
Only C (“Den anger vem som sköter tekniken.”) is mildly off-shape for a programme row, and that elimination is too soft to score.
A (“Den är märkt med slingans symbol.”) is an expert-only trap — the loop symbol belongs to hörselslinga, not to textning — and is invisible to a student.
Floor ≈ 30%.
justification: A clean detail item: no channel gives a student purchase, and the one knowledge-based elimination is expert-only and mild.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — ABSENT: the only proposition surviving across three of four Q2 options is that surtitled performances are a listed accessibility row in a season programme, and that is already supplied by Q2's own stem (“raden för textade föreställningar”). It kills no option in Q1. Q1 supplies nothing Q2 needs — Q1's options never touch the programme.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — ABSENT: there is no shared variable on which an option in each confirms the other. Q1 C (a count of “textade kvällar” to be increased) and Q2 D (a row's position in the listing) are merely consistent with one world, which is not vouching.
Joint stems-only floor ≈ 0.28 x 0.30 ≈ 8% against a 6.25% base — a negligible lift.
The pair is NOT jointly solvable.
justification: The two questions sit on different objects — a stance and a printed row — and neither option set pays for the other; this is the cleanest unit in the batch.

findings: 2+2 CONTRADICTORY ON ONE VARIABLE — scoreable: A and B are both hoof claims that contradict on whether the surface carried the horses (“Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick.” versus “Hovarna klarade sig med broddar.”), and C and D contradict on whether the horses were in this work at all. The whole set is organised on the single variable the stem asks about.

CROSS_QUESTION: three of four Q2 options presuppose repeated driven loads — “vändorna”, “ute och körde”, “sista lasset var hemma” — which kills D and pushes the pick onto the horses-worked side of the 2+2.
Residual genuine ambiguity: A survives the leak if the households hand-sledged the loads over a crust that bore people, which is a real Swedish winter-work motif — so the lift stops at the pair.
justification: A scoreable 2+2 plus a sibling-question leak takes the student from 25% to roughly half without reading a word of the passage.

findings: Mild stem-fit only: “hur arbetet lades upp” asks for an arrangement, and D (“Man fortsatte tills sista lasset var hemma.”) is a tempo fact rather than an arrangement; A, B and C are all arrangement-shaped and undifferentiated.
No absolutizer, no twin, no quantifier tic, and the Q1 option set supplies nothing this question needs — the leak in this unit runs the other way.
Floor ≈ 35%.
justification: One soft shape-based elimination against three equally live arrangements is not a scoreable channel.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — PRESENT and strong: the proposition that these weeks consisted of repeated driven loads survives across three of four Q2 options (“delade på vändorna”, “ute och körde”, “sista lasset var hemma”) and is supplied by neither stem — Q1's stem says only “Vad sägs i texten om hästarna?” and Q2's stem only that work was organised. It kills Q1 D (“Hästarna användes till annat under de veckorna.”) and weakens Q1 A, taking Q1 from 25% to about 50%.
No reverse leak: Q1's options add nothing Q2 needs, so the leak is strictly one-way, Q2 to Q1.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — PRESENT on the shared variable 'the horses drew the winter loads': Q1 C (“Hästarna drog kälken i stället.”) and Q2 C (“Barnen fick lasta medan de vuxna var ute och körde.”) each raise the other's probability, since driving loads home presupposes a team.
Joint stems-only floor ≈ 0.48 x 0.37 ≈ 18% against a 6.25% base, roughly three times base — the leakiest pair in the batch.
NOT jointly solvable (neither leg reaches 60%), but the leak is real and should be closed by de-specifying the driving vocabulary in Q2's distractors.
justification: A genuine one-way leak plus symmetric vouching on one shared variable roughly triples the joint stems-only floor; it does not reach joint solvability, so the pair is flagged rather than killed.
